Rampaging Ursaguana.text: Owned Bear: 6-mana haste trample ward, grows each attack. First in for a top-end slot.

Copper Host Crusher.text: 8/8 trample hexproof Bear; Goreclaw makes it 6. Top-end only.

Striped Bears.text: 4-mana Bear that draws a card; an Ayula trigger that replaces itself.

Fierce Witchstalker.text: In the deck now: 4-mana 4/4 trample Wolf and a Food; took Kogla's slot.

Howling Moon.text: +2/+2 to a Wolf each combat; Wolf tokens on their second spell.

Cemetery Prowler.text: 3-mana 3/4 Wolf; graveyard exile on enter/attack and a creature discount.

Werewolf Pack Leader.text: 2-mana 3/3 that draws when you attack with total power 6+ (F6). Not a Wolf.

Arlinn, Voice of the Pack.text: Six mana for a Wolf-token walker. Wolves entering with a counter helps the gate, but it is slow and its static does nothing for Bears.

Mayor of Avabruck // Howlpack Alpha.text: Wolf lord and Wolf maker once it flips; needs a turn with no spells.

The Great Henge.text: Owned: free with a 7-power creature out; taps for GG, counters and a card per creature.

Selvala, Heart of the Wilds.text: Owned: mana equal to greatest power, but it also draws the opponent cards.

Goliath, Mass Manipulator.text: Owned: power-up draws a card per power-4 creature.

Sylvan Scavenging.text: Owned: end-step counter, or a 3/3 if you control a power-4 creature.

Large Bear.text: In the deck now (Sarulf allows black).

Head of the Hunt.text: In the deck now: black Wolf; their dying creatures become your Wolves.

The Chief Warg.text: In the deck now: draws on each ferocious attack.

Chief Warg's Company.text: In the deck now: a Wolf every upkeep.

Garruk, Cursed Huntsman.text: In the deck now: two Wolves a turn or kill-and-draw.

Assassin's Trophy.text: In the deck now: removal that also feeds Sarulf.

Kogla, the Titan Ape.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: GGG 6-drop; black removal covers its fight.

Vivien Reid.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: black removal covers its answers.

Tovolar's Huntmaster // Tovolar's Packle.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: 6-mana Wolf maker.

Esika's Chariot.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: Cat tokens, crew 4.

Giant-Man, Gargantuan Genius.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: mana per power-4 creature.

Return of the Wildspeaker.text: Cut in the Sarulf rebuild: draw by greatest non-Human power, or a team pump.

Titania's Command.text: Two Bears (two Ayula triggers) plus counters on everything; 6 mana. Benched before.

Ursine Guide // Ranger's Merit.text: Already benched: its Bear Cub engine needs spells not from your starting deck.

Sauron, the Necromancer.text: Re-read in batch 4, unchanged. A 5-mana 4/4 menace (F2). Its attack trigger needs a creature card in YOUR graveyard, and that graveyard stays thin here: Sarulf's wipe exiles rather than bins, so only combat trades and the opponent's removal fill it (Mother Bear and Vastlands Scavenger add a few). Read the trigger as a bonus, the body as the card.

Flaxen Intruder // Welcome Home.text: Adventure makes three 2/2 Bears = three Ayula triggers (F1); the 1-drop half answers an artifact/enchantment.

Beorn's Hospitality.text: Landfall counters; becomes a land-count Bear for 7. Slow.

Owlbear Shepherd.text: Draws each end step when total power is 8+ — trivial with this board (F6). 3 MV (F3 risk).

Lukamina, Moon Druid.text: Re-graded in batch 4. Specialize (six lands, {3}, discard a green card or a Forest) makes Lukamina, Bear Form: a 4/4 trample Bear with 'other creatures you control get +1/+1 and have trample', so every 3-power Bear opens the gate (F2). The entry seek is a free land, and the form returns to base when it dies. Wolf Form needs a red discard, so it is out of reach in BG. Scorpion Form (black discard) is a deathtouch 4/4 that must be blocked.

Toski, Bearer of Secrets.text: Indestructible; a card whenever any creature connects (F6). Must attack as a 1/1, but indestructible.

Argoth, Sanctum of Nature.text: Untapped with a legendary green creature (Sarulf is one); {2}{G}{G}: a 2/2 Bear — an Ayula trigger mana sink. For a Forest.

Mirkwood.text: Tapped black-green dual that sacrifices for two counters on a Bear or Wolf. For a Forest.

Forebear's Blade.text: +3/+0 trample turns any 1-2 power body into a gate-opener (F2) and moves when it dies.

Nighthowl Pursuer.text: 1-drop Wolf that is a 3/3 menace attacker once the gate is on (consumer, F2).

Rhovanion Rampager.text: Sacrifices a creature to grow; the deck does not want to sacrifice its bodies.

Vincent Valentine.text: Counters equal to the power of each opposing creature that dies — 16 removal spells feed it; flips to trample lifelink.

Ascendant Packleader.text: 1-drop Wolf that grows on every 4+ MV spell (most of the deck). F3 risk.

Tenacious Pup.text: Cut once already: a 1/2 and a one-shot boon.

Packsong Pup.text: Grows by one a turn with another Wolf; small.

Torgal, A Fine Hound.text: Any-colour mana dork that is a Wolf; its Human clause is dead here.

Wargling.text: Gate consumer (deck 69 trimmed it for that reason).

Hound Tamer // Untamed Pup.text: Counter sink; night side gives Wolves trample. Day/night is fiddly.

Howlpack Resurgence.text: Flash Wolf anthem (+1/+1 trample) with 10 Wolves.

Shrill Howler // Howling Chorus.text: Evasion against small blockers; slow to flip.

Varis, Silverymoon Ranger.text: Ventures on creature casts; a dungeon completion makes one Wolf. Slow payoff.

Weaver of Blossoms // Blossom-Clad Werew.text: 3-mana mana creature; the deck has better ramp.

Garruk Relentless // Garruk, the Veil-Cu.text: Now legal (black-green): 3 damage to a creature, or a Wolf a turn; flips to deathtouch Wolves and a tutor.

Geistpack Alpha.text: 4-mana 5/4 trample Wolf — a gate-opener on arrival (F2), Goreclaw-discounted; dies into a seek.

Lupine Harbingers.text: 4/4 haste trample Wolf; foretold it grows.

Howlpack Piper // Wildsong Howler.text: Re-graded in batch 4. The engine of a no-spell turn: it puts a creature from hand onto the battlefield without casting it, so Bears still trigger Ayula on entry while the turn counts as spell-less. That makes it night, which flips Avabruck Caretaker and the Piper itself (look at six for a creature), and pays Nightpack Ambusher's and Edgar's end-step clauses. Untaps after a Wolf or Werewolf.

Mantle of the Wolf.text: +4/+4 makes a gate-opener; two Wolves when it leaves. An Aura.

Edgar, Moonlit Sovereign.text: Re-graded in batch 4. Flash, so cast it in the opponent's end step and pass your own turn with no spell: Edgar takes two counters, it becomes night, and Nightpack Ambusher (in the deck) makes a Wolf off the same clause. A 4/4 on arrival (F2), and {4}{G} spreads counters, which Constrictor and Hardened Scales add to.

Sage of Ancient Lore // Werewolf of Anci.text: Draws one on entry, and its size is your hand size, so it is small in a deck that empties its hand. Werewolf, not Wolf.

Avabruck Caretaker // Hollowhenge Huntma.text: A hexproof 4/4 that puts two counters on another creature each combat, which turns a 2-power Bear into a gate-opener (F2). Its night side puts two counters on everything and gives the rest of the board hexproof: the deck's best protection card in the pile. MV 6, so it survives most Sarulf wipes (F3).

Flourishing Hunter.text: A 6/6 Wolf body that gains some life. A Wolf count of one for six mana; the deck has better six-drops.

Wolfkin Outcast // Wedding Crasher.text: Costs four with a Wolf out (the deck has 10). 5/4 for the gate; its night side draws when Wolves die. Werewolf type, so it is not itself a Wolf.

Somberwald Beastmaster.text: Seven mana for four bodies (a Wolf, a 3/3 and a 4/4 among them), and the tokens have deathtouch. Tokens are MV 0, so a Sarulf wipe takes all of them (F3).

Primal Witchstalker.text: A 3-mana BG Wolf with menace that ramps a land back from a mill of four. Cheap Wolf count (F4); the deck already runs Fierce Witchstalker.

Sword of Body and Mind.text: +2/+2 turns any 2-power creature into a power-4 gate-opener (F2), protection from green covers the mirror, and a hit makes a Wolf (F4). MV 3, so it is exposed to a big Sarulf wipe.

Fuel Tank Feaster.text: A 2-mana any-colour dork (Alchemy) that discounts your biggest creature each turn. The deck has three dorks already; a fourth is only worth it if the ramp suite is cut back elsewhere.

Fight Rigging.text: A counter on a creature every combat (F2 enabler), plus a free hideaway card once you have power 7. Big Bears, Lumra and Vaultborn reach 7. Repeatable and cheap.

Flare of Cultivation.text: Ramp that can be free by sacrificing a nontoken green creature. The deck has 6 ramp spells plus Sarulf to protect; a sacrifice cost on a creature deck is a real cost.

Descendants' Path.text: A free creature each upkeep when the top card shares a type with your board. With 37 creatures, about 37% of draws are creatures, and most share Bear or Wolf. Lands and noncreature spells whiff and go to the bottom.

World War Hulk.text: Chapter I makes the next green creature free, chapter II gives three counters (a 1-power Bear becomes a gate-opener, F2), chapter III doubles power with trample. A strong turn-5 play in a creature deck.

Omnipresence.text: Eight mana. The deck wins by the time this resolves.

Etali, Primal Garden.text: A 7/7 trampler (Alchemy) that casts a random Dinosaur free on entry and attack. Real value, but off-tribe, and actualize barely discounts it here.

Heirloom Epic.text: Tapping creatures to draw is slow in a deck that wants to attack with them.

Monstrous Vortex.text: Fires on power-5+ creature spells; the deck runs 8 (Beorns, Big Bears, Surrak and Goreclaw, Chief Warg's Company, Vaultborn, Rhonas). A free spell on each, but 8 of 37 creatures is a thin trigger.

Path of Discovery.text: Every creature explores: a land in hand or a +1/+1 counter. That counter takes a 3-power Bear to 4 (F2), and with 37 creatures it is repeatable card advantage (F6).

Chimil, the Inner Sun.text: A free MV-5-or-less card every end step (F6, repeatable), and your spells can't be countered. MV 6 colourless, so it survives most Sarulf wipes (F3).

Sentinel of the Nameless City.text: A 3-mana 3/4 vigilance that makes a Map on entry and every attack. Each Map is an explore, which means a counter or a land. Strong 3-drop, though not a Bear.

Mole Man, Moloid Master.text: A landfall token maker. The deck has no landfall plan.

Wrenn and Realmbreaker.text: Fixing the deck does not need. The +1 is a 3/3 attacker and the -2 digs for a permanent. Fine, not a fit.

Icetill Explorer.text: A landfall and graveyard-lands engine; off plan.

Elemental Teachings.text: Five mana for two tapped lands.

World Shaper.text: A lands-recursion payoff with no lands plan behind it.

Nissa, Vital Force.text: A 5/5 haste land each turn, which is a gate-opener (F2), and -3 regrows a permanent. A playable five-drop walker.

Ancient Greenwarden.text: Doubles landfall triggers the deck does not have. A 5/7 reach body is all it gives.

Kamahl's Druidic Vow.text: Sarulf satisfies the legendary-sorcery rule, and the deck has about 15 legendary permanents plus lands. An X spell that puts several onto the battlefield; strong late, weak early.

Nog, Ambitious Cadet.text: A Ferengi with a land-recursion mode. Off plan.

Nissa of Shadowed Boughs.text: BG walker that grows from land drops; its -5 puts a creature onto the battlefield with two counters. Slow to get there.

Badlands Revival.text: Two-for-one recursion after removal. Sarulf exiles rather than sends to the graveyard, so it does not undo a wipe.

Glacier Godmaw.text: A 6/6 trampler whose landfall pumps the team and gives haste. Seven mana; a finisher the deck does not need.

Berserk.text: Doubles a creature's power for one swing, then kills it if it attacked. One big hit for a creature you lose.

Burgeoning.text: One-opponent Brawl gives about one extra land a turn cycle. Not the deck's problem.

Glimpse of Nature.text: A burst-draw turn needs a hand of cheap creatures; this deck's creatures cost 3–5.

Hunter's Axe.text: One mana, +2/+0: a 2-power Bear becomes a gate-opener (F2). Equip {2} each time, and the Sword and Forebear's Blade do the same job better.

Vraska, Swarm's Eminence.text: A deathtouch-token planeswalker. The deck has few deathtouch creatures.

Vraska, Golgari Queen.text: -3 destroys a nonland permanent with MV 3 or less, and +2 trades a spare permanent for a card. A fair replacement removal piece if one is cut (F5).

Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler.text: Dorks and tap abilities work the turn they enter; -2 returns a 2-drop Bear. Modest.

Chevill, Bane of Monsters.text: A 2-mana deathtouch body that marks one opposing creature at a time and draws when it dies. With 16 removal spells and Ayula fights it is a repeatable draw (F6).

Fiend Artisan.text: A creature tutor that needs a sacrifice. It can find Ayula or Goreclaw, but its size reads your graveyard and Sarulf exiles rather than bins.

Insidious Roots.text: Tokens tap for mana and Plants grow when creature cards leave the graveyard. Off plan.

Vraska Joins Up.text: Deathtouch counters on the team on entry, then a card whenever a legendary creature connects. About 14 legendary creatures here; the counters are not +1/+1 and do not open the gate.

Winding Constrictor.text: Every counter you place gets one more. Ayula's two counters become three, Fight Rigging and Avabruck give more, and Sarulf itself gets two per opposing permanent instead of one, so its wipe charges twice as fast. A 2-mana 2/3.

Dina, Essence Brewer.text: A sacrifice outlet. The deck has no sacrifice plan.

Kraven the Hunter.text: A 3-mana 4/3 trampler (power 4 on arrival, F2) that draws and grows whenever the opponent's biggest creature dies. Removal and fights trigger it. Note: Head of the Hunt (in the deck) exiles dying creatures instead, which switches Kraven off.

Sméagol, Helpful Guide.text: Needs one of your creatures to die each turn.

Beifong's Bounty Hunters.text: A 4/4 for 4 (F2) that turns each dying creature into a land creature with counters equal to its power. A sturdy body.

Culling Ritual.text: Destroys every nonland permanent with MV 2 or less, including your own dorks, 2-drop Bears and Constrictor. Sarulf already gives the deck a wipe.

Host of the Hereafter.text: A 4/4 for 4 whose counters move to another creature when it dies. Fine, not exciting.

Jenova, Ancient Calamity.text: Gives counters equal to its own power, which starts at 1. Needs a pump first.

Mortality Spear.text: An instant that destroys any nonland permanent. Four mana here, since the deck rarely gains life. A fair replacement removal piece (F5).

Kagha, Shadow Archdruid.text: Graveyard casting off a mill of two. Off plan.

Rise of the Witch-king.text: An edict that also costs you a creature, then returns a permanent. Symmetrical in a creature deck.

Deathbloom Ritualist.text: Its mana scales with creature cards in your graveyard; this deck's graveyard stays small.

Diregraf Rebirth.text: Reanimation with flashback. Undoes removal, but not a Sarulf wipe, which exiles.

Lord of Extinction.text: Its size reads all graveyards; Sarulf exiles, so graveyards stay small here.

Ygra, Eater of All.text: A 6/6 for 5 (F2) that grows whenever a creature dies. It also gives every opposing creature a 'sacrifice: gain 3 life' ability, which helps the opponent (owner's rule).

Back for More.text: Instant reanimation plus a fight, for six mana.

Mycoid Resurrection.text: Graveyard reanimation; the graveyard stays thin here.

The Last Ronin.text: Chapter I destroys every creature, and this is a 37-creature deck.

Harness Infinity.text: Swaps hand and graveyard for six mana with a BBB GGG cost. A graveyard deck's card.

Vraska, Regal Gorgon.text: Seven mana. -3 destroys a creature and +2 opens the gate (F2), but the deck has cheaper removal.

Witherbloom, the Balancer.text: Affinity for creatures, so about 3 mana on a normal board, for a 5/5 flying deathtouch. It also gives instants and sorceries affinity, which discounts the removal. MV 8, so a Sarulf wipe never takes it (F3).

Old Stickfingers.text: An X spell that fills the graveyard; its size reads creature cards there.

Cursebound Witch.text: A 1/2 that drafts a card from its spellbook when it dies (Alchemy). Low impact in a 100-card creature deck.

Dark Ritual.text: One burst of BBB for a card. Only black spells use it, and the deck's power is green.

Vraska, Betrayal's Sting.text: 0: draw a card and proliferate, every turn, which adds a counter to every creature with one, to Sarulf (a bigger wipe) and to Vraska. Repeatable draw (F6). Six mana. Its -2 turns a creature into a Treasure the OPPONENT keeps, which gives them mana, so it clashes with the owner's removal rule; treat it as a draw-and-proliferate walker.

Vat Emergence.text: Reanimate from ANY graveyard, so it can steal the creature your removal just killed, then proliferate. Five mana.

Cankerbloom.text: A 2-mana 3/2 that sacrifices to destroy an artifact or enchantment, or to proliferate. A flexible noncreature answer on a body.

Unnatural Restoration.text: Two mana: regrow a permanent card and proliferate. Fine value, small.

Evolution Sage.text: Proliferate on every land drop, twice with Evolving Wilds, Fabled Passage or Prismatic Vista. Grows the Ayula-counter Bears and charges Sarulf each turn. A 3/2 for 3.

Urban Daggertooth.text: A 4/3 vigilance for 4 (F2). Proliferates whenever it is dealt damage, which a fight or a block does.

Hardened Scales.text: One mana: each +1/+1 counter placement on a creature gets one more: Ayula's two become three, and Sarulf's counters count. It stacks with Winding Constrictor. MV 1, so every Sarulf wipe takes it (F3).

Mythweaver Poq.text: Its size is your land count (power 4+ by turn four, F2), and each turn it conjures a copy of the land you played, so a fetch land is played twice. Ramp on a body, Alchemy.

Stable Wormhole.text: A tapped any-colour land token every time you attack. The deck has enough ramp; this is ramp that needs the attack first.
